title: aidd eval worlds
description: The format of evals/worlds.json: the worlds an eval case's project can be set in. A world is a programming language and a business domain, with a small project that builds it, so the cases are not all set in the one world their author knew. A live case names its world in a `world:<name>` tag. The file also holds the share of the live cases any one world, language, or domain may have, and the shares that are over it today.

cap.description: The most any one world, language, or domain may have of the live cases, as a share.

languages.description: Each programming language a world may use, with the file names and suffixes that show a project holds it. `none` is a project with no source file. Markup, styles, and shell scripts show no language.

markers.description: A suffix, such as `.py`, or a file name, such as `package.json`. A project holds the language when one of its files has a marker.

worlds.description: Each world by its name, `<language>-<domain>`, in the order of the languages, then the domains.

language.description: A key of `languages`: the one language the world's project is written in.

domain.description: What the world's project is about, such as `commerce`. `general` says it is about no business.

means.description: What the world's project is, in one sentence.

seed.description: The script that builds the world's project in an empty folder, as a case's `fixture.sh` does.

risk.description: What `aidd risk --paths` says of planned paths in the built project: each row is one run and the route it must give.

over_cap.description: The worlds, languages, and domains that have more than `cap` of the live cases today, each with its case count. A count may only fall, and a row goes when its count is under the cap.
